items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: And I left him after we came back from Europe. After we came back from Europe he thought he was Toscanini, you know? And of course I resented that, and Shiman -- we could have gone to work that following week after we got off the boat, in he Apollo. He turned it down.

ctx.x: Chick just had this natural born knack of putting it together. Putting it together. You know, he could really put it together, which most band leaders don't have. And Teddy Hill, he didn't really have that, the musicians, you know. But he was a person -- he thought that -- he was just the opposite of a man who -- if you have an organization, whatever it be, a musical organization or whatever, and you have to have people -- you're supposed to surround yourself with the best talent you can get. You know, if you had…

singer with the band and this was during the time Maxine Sullivan came up with "Loch Lomond". "Loch Lomond" was a big hit. Any band that was playing at that time had to play "Loch Lomond." So Teddy's band -- we were playing this theater in Philadelphia, I think it was the Lincoln Theater, and so this girl sang "Loch Lomond" and locked up the show. They wouldn't let us off the stage, just from her singing "Loch Lomond". And do you know Teddy fired her. You wouldn't believe it. But that's the type of man he was.…
